profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting in an ML research lab between the person leading distributed systems work and the person leading ASR modeling work for an internal reproduction-and-extension study on distributed training of deep neural network acoustic models. The team is preparing a shared experiment package for a lab-wide checkpoint review next Wednesday, where the systems side needs a stable training interface and the modeling side needs comparable recognition outputs. The agenda is to align on what artifact will be handed off by Friday, which run configuration will be treated as the common baseline, how intermediate results should be logged, and who updates the shared experiment sheet. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on a Friday handoff, a baseline run to compare against, a common definition of readiness, and a plan for posting results and checkpoints to shared storage.

members.name: Nina Rao
members.expertise: Multi-GPU training, MPI/NCCL integration, mixed-precision optimization, cluster job orchestration
members.background: Nina has spent the last four years adapting large-scale training pipelines to HPC environments and usually owns performance benchmarking and reproducible job launch configurations for speech and vision projects.
members.private_state: She wants the coordination meeting to lock in a lightweight, reproducible handoff so she can finish scaling experiments on the cluster without getting pulled into model-analysis work; she is also worried about wasting expensive GPU time on runs that are not considered 'comparable' later.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'baseline run' in this project, they mean the current distributed recipe with the agreed code path but executed at 8 GPUs and normalized back to the single-node reference settings.
A run is 'ready' for handoff once training has completed, the checkpoint loads, and scalar training/validation curves are logged in the shared tracker; decoding and WER analysis happen downstream.
The 'Friday handoff' means that artifacts are uploaded to shared storage by end of day Pacific time because the HPC jobs and storage team operate on that schedule.
Updating the 'experiment sheet' means adding one row per training job with throughput, final loss, and checkpoint path, not attaching per-subset decoding outputs.

members.name: Leo Martens
members.expertise: Acoustic modeling, lattice-free training, decoding pipelines, benchmark evaluation for speech recognition
members.background: Leo came from a speech-focused research group where reproducibility centered on benchmark-comparable decoding outputs and carefully versioned recipes derived from public ASR toolkits.
members.private_state: He wants the meeting to preserve scientific comparability with prior ASR results and ensure the distributed work produces outputs he can immediately use in the review deck; he is concerned that systems-side optimizations may shift training behavior in ways that are hard to explain later.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'baseline run' for acoustic modeling, they mean the canonical single-process recipe from the public benchmark setup that previous WER numbers were reported from, even if distributed training is used to accelerate it.
A run is only 'ready' if it includes standard dev-set decoding and a WER number, because training loss alone is not a meaningful deliverable for ASR comparison.
The 'Friday handoff' means artifacts are available before his early Saturday script window on the shared server, effectively Friday night UTC, since he often lets evaluation jobs roll overnight.
The 'experiment sheet' is the team-facing record for comparison, so each row should include decoded dev-clean/dev-other style outputs, scoring notes, and any recipe deviations.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the baseline run
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the baseline' or 'baseline run' as if it were a single agreed reference.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the current distributed training reference configuration in the new codebase: 8-GPU data-parallel training with gradient accumulation chosen to match the effective batch size of the older single-node setup.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the canonical benchmark recipe that produced prior ASR comparison numbers: the original single-process training setup and its associated decoding recipe, regardless of whether the new system accelerates it underneath.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both think 'baseline' is already socially established by prior project discussions, and because they are coordinating handoffs rather than debating model design, each treats the phrase as obvious shorthand instead of something that needs unpacking.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say a run should be 'ready' or 'good to share' by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes readiness means the training job completed successfully, the final checkpoint and logs are uploaded, and the run can be resumed or inspected by others.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes readiness means there is at least one standard dev-set decode with scored WER and enough metadata to compare against prior acoustic-model results.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML coordination meetings, saying something is 'ready' usually sounds routine and uncontroversial; both assume the other person naturally includes the same downstream steps that are standard in their own subfield.

misalignment_points.topic: Boundary of the shared results sheet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'put it in the experiment sheet' after the run finishes.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the sheet is a systems tracking artifact containing job IDs, config hashes, throughput, convergence summaries, and checkpoint locations for all distributed runs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the sheet is the scientific comparison table for the review, so entries should include decoding outputs, WER, and notes on which benchmark scoring setup was used.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase refers to a real shared spreadsheet both use, but different tabs and conventions have evolved around it; during a quick coordination call, 'put it in the sheet' feels sufficiently specific because neither thinks the tab-level boundary needs mentioning.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both commit to having the handoff done 'by Friday'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes Friday means by end of business Friday Pacific, aligned with cluster allocation resets and her normal upload/check-in routine.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes Friday means available before his overnight evaluation window starts, effectively late Friday UTC so that he can decode before the weekend review prep.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The difference is small enough to sound pedantic, both are being cooperative, and academic teams often use informal weekday deadlines without restating timezone or cutoff unless a conflict is already anticipated.
